Draw the Path on the viewer for one canyon (each point can make it deeper or wider there), or leave it empty for a network of canyons, Scale apart, winding across the terrain with side canyons (Branches). Width is the canyon's width at the rim, Floor the share of it that is flat bottom, Steps how many ledges the rock beds make in its walls. Feed it a plateau (a Mesas node, a Constant) through Height.

valley.glacial.description: A U-shaped valley a glacier carved, along a line drawn on the terrain: a wide flat floor gently descending between steep walls. Draw the Path on the viewer (each point can make it wider there). Floor height is the height of its flat floor where the path starts, Drop how much lower it lies at the end; Width is the valley's width from rim to rim, Floor the share of it that is flat, Steepness how sheer its walls are. Cut it into mountains through Height for a valley like Yosemite or Lauterbrunnen; a floor under the sea level makes a fjord.

water.rivers.description: Rivers where enough of the land drains, their beds and banks dug into the relief, wider and deeper downstream, holding lakes in deep hollows. Follows the rain to the sea or the terrain's edge and lays a river wherever enough land drains: a thread at its source, wider and deeper as water joins it. Its water only ever goes down, cutting through the rims of shallow hollows and filling deep ones with lakes. Threshold sets how many rivers there are; Width and Depth those of the largest; Banks how gently the land slopes down to them. Water already on the map (wired to Water) is kept, and rivers end where they reach it.

wind.erosion.description: The wind blows loose sand into dunes, ridged where sand is plenty and crescents where it is scarce, and wears bare rock that faces it. Spreads Sand blocks of loose sand (where the Sand mask says) and lets the wind work it: it lifts sand in the open, carries it a hop downwind, and drops it in the lee of every rise, so that dunes grow with gentle backs to the wind and steep slip faces away from it. Plenty of sand makes transverse ridges; little makes barchans. Abrasion wears rock facing the wind into streamlined ridges (yardangs). Connect a wind vector (Climate's wind) to make the wind turn over the land.
